content:
#1 I was trying to understand Chen’s iterated integrals a bit more abstractly and ran into the following confusion about loop spaces.

Let XXX be a smooth manifold, viewed as a simplicial presheaf over Mfld\text{Mfld}Mfld or CartSp\text{CartSp}CartSp. It seems to me there are two different notions of the free loop space of XXX. The first is what’s described on free loop space object. This is as the powering XS1X^{S^1}XS1 or alternatively as the internal hom [LConst(S1),X][\text{LConst}(S^1), X][LConst(S1),X]. The second is the internal hom [S1,X][S^1, X][S1,X] where here S1S^1S1 is the usual smooth manifold under Yoneda.

These two notions seem to be quite different — roughly, the first does not seem to remember the smooth structure on S1S^1S1. Is that true? (for instance the global sections seem to be different…) How are these two objects related?
subject: Two notions of the free loop space

content:
#2 Indeed, this is a crucial difference.

Notice that if by XXX you always mean the presheaf Rn↦C∞(Rn,X)\mathbb{R}^n \mapsto C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n, X)Rn↦C∞(Rn,X), then in fact [LConst(S1),X]=X[\mathrm{LConst}(S^1), X] = X[LConst(S1),X]=X, since there are then no non-trivial morphisms in XXX, and so the the non-trivial morphism in LConst(S1)\mathrm{LConst}(S^1)LConst(S1) necessarily goes to the identity on some point.

So the issue is that XXX exists in different modes: once as a smooth manifold (which has possibly non-trivial smooth structure but only trivial morphisms), once as its shape or path infinity-groupoid ʃX≔LConstΠ∞(X)ʃ X \coloneqq {\mathrm{LConst}} \Pi_\infty(X)ʃX:=LConstΠ∞​(X) (which has trivial smooth structure but possibly non-trivial morphisms).

Same for the circle S1S^1S1 itself. And similar then for the loop space: there is the smooth loop space [S1,X][S^1, X][S1,X] (smooth structure, no morphisms), and the free loop space of the homotopy type [ʃS1,ʃX][ʃ S^1, ʃ X][ʃS1,ʃX] (morphisms, no smooth structure).

The relation should be

ʃ[S1,X]  ≃  [ʃS1,ʃX] ʃ[S^1, X] \;\simeq\; [ʃ S^1, ʃ X] ʃ[S1,X]≃[ʃS1,ʃX]

(by the statement in… let’s see, section 4.2 in arXiv:math/0612096)
subject: Two notions of the free loop space

As you said the target is discrete so all that matters is the zero-simplices of the domain. Got it!)

My motivation for asking was the following confusion in trying to understand Chen’s iterated integrals abstractly.

Chen’s iterated integrals, at least as explained by Getzler, Jones, and Petrack, can be written as a transgression-type procedure (see the top of page 13): in weight kkk,

  1. first pullback your (k+1)(k+1)(k+1) differential forms from Xk+1X^{k+1}Xk+1 to LX×Δk\mathrm{LX}\times \Delta^kLX×Δk under the evaluation map sending (ℓ,t1,…,tk)↦(ℓ(0),ℓ(t1),…,ℓ(tk))(\ell, t_1,\ldots,t_k)\mapsto (\ell(0),\ell(t_1),\ldots,\ell(t_k))(ℓ,t1​,…,tk​)↦(ℓ(0),ℓ(t1​),…,ℓ(tk​))

  2. then integrate out the simplex directions via the projection LX×Δk→LX\mathrm{LX} \times \Delta^k \to {\mathrm{LX}}LX×Δk→LX These fit together to yield map of chain complexes C(Ω∗X,Ω∗X)→Ω∗(LX)C(\Omega^*X, \Omega^*X)\to\Omega^*(\mathrm{LX})C(Ω∗X,Ω∗X)→Ω∗(LX) essentially because of the families Stokes theorem.

A less ad hoc interpretation of this construction is that we are choosing a cosimplicial model for the free loop space LX∙\mathrm{LX}^\bulletLX∙ coming from the standard simplicial circle (hence the Xk+1X^{k+1}Xk+1 appearing) and then studying the pullback by the evaluation map (of cosimplicial objects) Δ∙×Tot(LX∙)→LX∙=X∙+1\Delta^\bullet\times \text{Tot}(\mathrm{LX}^\bullet) \to {\mathrm{LX}}^\bullet=X^{\bullet+1}Δ∙×Tot(LX∙)→LX∙=X∙+1 followed by fiber integration. This is exactly how Jones sets up the corresponding map for singular cochains.

If I want to make the previous paragraph precise for differential forms I might choose to work in simplicial presheaves so that I can make sense of the free loop space and differential forms on it. But now I am a bit concerned that the loop space appearing in the construction above is only seeing S1S^1S1 simplicially… shouldn’t we be considering the smooth loop space [S1,X][S^1, X][S1,X]? I think I’m missing something very basic here.

content:
#15 Re #11:

But what would be better is a version of the theorem where the map lives in the category of diffeological spaces, but where the fibres are honest manifolds with boundary. This would cover the case of Fréchet manifolds that I was considering, but also other cases of interest for people around here.

Doesn’t this follow automatically from the case of bases being ordinary manifolds? If F is a typical fiber (a smooth manifold with boundary), denote by Ω^n_F the moduli stack of bundles with a typical fiber F (dim F = k) whose total space is equipped with a differential n-form.

Then fiberwise integration yields morphisms A: Ω^n_F→Ω^{n−k} and B: Ω^n_{∂F}→Ω^{n−k+1}, as well as i*: Ω^n_F→Ω^n_{∂F}, d_F: Ω^n_F→Ω^{n+1}_F, and d: Ω^{n−k}→Ω^{n−k+1}.

Thus, we have a formula d∘A = A∘d_F ± B∘i* on the level of sheaves of abelian groups. Diffeological spaces embed into sheaves of sets fully faithfully, so taking hom from a diffeological space will give you what you want.
subject: Two notions of the free loop space
